candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — provide caregiver education that promotes infant growth, development, nutrition, and safe home care
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — infant formula preparation safety
candidate.educational_objective: Prepare powdered infant formula using the exact manufacturer-specified water-to-powder ratio, measuring water first and avoiding intentional dilution or concentration.

options.A: Measure the exact amount of water listed on the formula container first, then add the directed amount of powder
options.B: Add extra water to each bottle so the formula is easier for the infant's kidneys to handle
options.C: Add extra powder when the infant seems hungry so the bottle provides more calories
options.D: Estimate the water-to-powder ratio by bottle size rather than following the container directions

candidate.rationale: CDC's May 2026 guidance says to follow the infant-formula container instructions exactly when preparing powdered formula. For most healthy infants using a safe water source, measure the specified water first and then add the directed powder. Too much water can dilute nutrition, while too little water can overconcentrate the formula and contribute to dehydration or excessive renal/digestive workload. Extra hot-water precautions apply to specific higher-risk infants and are not a universal rule for all formula preparation. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Powdered infant formula should be mixed exactly according to container directions using safe water, with water measured before powder; intentional over- or under-dilution can harm the infant.
candidate.source_locator: Preparation: use water from a safe source; use the amount of water listed on the formula-container instructions; always measure water first and then add powder; too much water may not meet nutritional needs and too little water can contribute to dehydration. 'Different recommendations' section distinguishes routine preparation from extra precautions for infants <2 months, premature infants, or infants with weakened immunity
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A parent is preparing powdered infant formula for a healthy full-term infant using a safe household water source. Which action is correct?
